ledger.claim: The route actually driven was not the recommended route. The trip record logs route_deviation_detected at 11:30:14 at New Upper Changi Road / Jalan Bilal (recommended Bedok Road, vehicle took Jalan Bilal) and route_rejoined at 11:35:16 at Upper East Coast Road / Siglap Road, and the driver's own trace puts ten consecutive fixes on Jalan Bilal and five on Siglap Road before the rejoin - the 'small roads near Siglap' the rider complains of. The rider's factual account is corroborated by the platform's own telemetry, not merely asserted.

Under POL-RD-21 the driver had to inform the rider of the deviation by in-app chat - or verbally with the trip call recording as evidence - before or at the point of deviation. The chat log is complete and holds only two messages, both at 11:26-11:27 and both about the taxi stand, i.e. before the 11:28:02 trip start; the trip record's messages_during_trip block is empty and in_app_calls is empty. So no chat notice was given and there is no call recording in the record, and the deviation at 11:30:14 was unannounced and unagreed. Any asserted verbal notice cannot be established under POL-RD-21 read with POL-GEN-26.

POL-RD-23 requires traffic data for the recommended segment at the trip time showing congestion, an incident or a closure. The LTA advisory for Bedok Road across the trip window (valid 10:58-12:28) reports type NONE, 'no incident, roadwork or closure', and speed bands 4-6 throughout. 'Bus stop and traffic light very long' is not one of POL-RD-23's types (closure, congestion, incident), and the driver's claim that the Siglap side is 'about the same distance' is contradicted by the recorded distances. The reroute is therefore not traffic-justified, which closes the traffic-justified rows (a), (b) and (c) of POL-RD-24 and leaves the driver with no justification for departing the recommended route at all.

Honest concession, and the rider does not stretch the record to avoid it. POL-RD-22 makes the platform's recorded distances the measure and forbids re-measuring from the trace; on those recorded distances the deviation is 5.2 - 4.6 = 0.60 km, which is inside POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. The two matrix rows that pay the excess distance fare - (b) and (d) - each require a deviation over 1 km and are therefore not available to the rider on this evidence, and the excess distance fare itself (0.60 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.43 SGD, not the 2.00 SGD pleaded, on POL-RD-24's formula) is not recoverable within tolerance. The rider's complaint is an unauthorised, unannounced detour, and that is the finding the record supports; the rider does not ask the tribunal to re-measure the route or to award a remedy POL-RD-24 does not provide.

The recorded deviation on this trip is 0.60 km: the platform's actual distance of 5.2 km minus its optimal distance of 4.6 km, exactly as POL-RD-22 directs (trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km). POL-RD-22 sets the tolerance at 1.0 km, so this reroute is within tolerance. Under POL-RD-24(e) a deviation of 1 km or less draws NO_ACTION, and the recorded distances are on the face of the trip record, so there is nothing for the rider to recover.

The LTA advisory for Bedok Road records type NONE and states no incident, roadwork or closure for the queried segment and window, so the reroute is not traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. That does not assist the rider: POL-RD-24's refund rows are keyed to distance as well as justification, and row (d) — refund of the excess distance fare — applies only where the deviation exceeds 1 km. At 0.60 km tolerance governs, not justification, so row (e) gives NO_ACTION.

The amount the rider could recover on any reading of POL-RD-24 is the excess distance fare — 0.60 km at the metered rate of 0.72 SGD per km, which is 0.43 SGD, computed without surge and rounded to the cent. The rider has asked for 2.00 SGD. The claim overstates the maximum conceivable sum by more than four times, and on the correct row (e) the sum is zero.

The GPS trace shows only which route was taken and when: it runs New Upper Changi Road, Jalan Bilal, Siglap Road, Upper East Coast Road, Marine Parade Road, and marks the deviation at Jalan Bilal and the rejoin at Upper East Coast Road. POL-RD-22 expressly directs that the trace is not used to re-measure the distance, because a sparse trace understates a route's length — its 4.315 km figure is below even the recommended 4.6 km and cannot displace the recorded 5.2 km. The recorded distances are the measure, and they give 0.60 km.

The chat log holds two messages, both sent and read before the trip started at 11:28, so the record contains no in-trip notice of the deviation under POL-RD-21. POL-RD-24 nonetheless draws no distinction on notification where the deviation is 1 km or less: rows (c) and (e) both give NO_ACTION. The notification question therefore does not change the outcome, and the metered fare stands either way.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03: it preserves the present payment state, and whether it helps the driver depends on who filed and where the money sits. The rider filed this dispute, the fare is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so NO_ACTION leaves the 9.42 SGD charge standing and the driver loses nothing. It is not a remedy that restores or returns any part of the fare.

This is a case the AI may decide finally. The contested amount is 2.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold at which an AI ruling is final at any confidence, and neither party's profile carries a fraud flag (both show 0), so the 0.95 confidence band is not engaged. Every fact POL-RD-24 needs — the recorded distances, the fare lines, the chat log, the traffic advisory and the GPS trace — is on the record in COMPLETE artifacts, so no open question arises under POL-GEN-26 and there is no basis to hold the fare by escalating it.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and Driver, the claim is decided on the recorded route and distances. The recommended route was New Upper Changi Road, Bedok Road, Upper East Coast Road and Marine Parade Road, 4.6 km. The route actually driven was New Upper Changi Road, Jalan Bilal, Siglap Road, Upper East Coast Road and Marine Parade Road, 5.2 km. The trip record and GPS fixes support the rider's account that the vehicle left Bedok Road at Jalan Bilal and rejoined at Siglap Road. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is the recorded actual distance minus the recorded optimal distance: 5.2 km minus 4.6 km equals 0.60 km. POL-RD-22 sets a 1.0 km tolerance, so this deviation is within tolerance. The GPS trace's 4.315 km figure is not used to re-measure distance under POL-RD-22; it shows the route taken only. The LTA traffic advisory for Bedok Road during the trip window reports type NONE, no incident, roadwork or closure, and speed bands 4-6, so POL-RD-23 does not justify the reroute. The chat log is complete and contains no in-trip notice or acknowledgment of the deviation, and there is no call recording, so POL-RD-21's notice requirement was not met. Even so, because the deviation is 1.0 km or less, POL-RD-24(e) applies: a not-traffic-justified deviation within tolerance gives NO_ACTION. The excess distance fare on POL-RD-24's formula would be 0.60 km x 0.72 SGD per km, which is 0.43 SGD, not the 2.00 SGD claimed, and it is not payable within tolerance. The 9.42 SGD metered fare stands. NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves the present state in place, with no refund to the rider and no driver compensation. The disputed value is 2.00 SGD and neither profile has a fraud flag; POL-RD-25 requires 0.80 confidence for a route deviation and the confidence here is 0.95 on complete weight-1.0 artifacts. No clause produces a referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
